_target_platform_rationale: GB10 / DGX Spark, compute 12.1, is the hardware every artifact built through this generic CB profile is for; sm_89 and sm_120 have their own exact producer profiles. Declared here because lane-eligibility v3 cells are PLATFORM-SCOPED and ServingLaneSpec.route_status_for refuses to match a cell without one -- a profile that names no platform resolves every unit UNATTESTED with source no_target_platform, which is fail-closed but says nothing useful. Naming sm_121 makes the answer legible instead: under the pinned Gridbook 0.9.1 the v12 table publishes CB cells on sm_89 and sm_120 only and on sm_121 publishes trellis cells alone, so a CB unit here resolves unattested with source no_cell and cb_route_status_gate REFUSES the export. That is correct and deliberate. Both CB compile preflights fix their capability in code (sm89_preflight.SM89_CAPABILITY = (8, 9), sm120_preflight.SM120_CAPABILITY = (12, 0)), so Gridbook has no CB receipt for compute 12.1 to publish, and principle 14 forbids transcribing one we merely believe. The escape hatches are the declared ones and both are stamped on the shipcard: PQ_CB_NON_NATIVE_TARGET, or PQ_CB_ROUTE_STATUS_OVERRIDE with the reason this artifact ships anyway. Remove neither this field nor the refusal to make a build pass -- the refusal IS the serving gap being reported (principle 1 carve-out, principle 9).
description: NVFP4-CB / FP8-CB codebook container lane: the separately released Gridbook vLLM plugin (immutable pin in prismaquant/gridbook_runtime/gridbook_runtime_pin.json; registered under quant_method 'gridbook', with the pre-rename 'prismaquant' key kept as a read alias for already-shipped artifacts) decodes the codebook schemes into NVFP4/FP8 buffers and delegates plain NVFP4/FP8/BF16 layers to stock compressed-tensors. PrismaQuant contains no runtime copy. Deliberately a MIXED container (PLAN.md decision #1, 'FP8 in every recipe'): CB rungs coexist with plain NVFP4, FP8_DYNAMIC and BF16 in one artifact. This generic profile also retains source-passthrough entries required to read and reproduce published source-model artifacts; their presence is compatibility coverage, not maintained performance eligibility for every target. Exact hardware producer profiles must close their own candidate surface. The scheme vocabulary is prismaquant-custom (NOT stock compressed-tensors, whose schemes cannot express codebooks); ships via prismaquant.export_nvfp4_cb, docs/lanes/nvfp4-cb/LAYOUT.md is the byte contract.

export_lane.detail: The serializer/compatibility surface remains the structural upper bound: NVFP4_CB_K1..K25, FP8_CB_K4,K8,...,K48, delegated NVFP4/FP8_DYNAMIC, FP8_SOURCE, and BF16. Serializer reachability is not target performance eligibility: exact hardware profiles narrow this inventory, and the maintained SM120/RTX50 profile explicitly denies W8A16/source-FP8 carriers while generic compatibility readers remain intact. NVFP4_CB_K26..K32 have no public parser, registry, contract, chooser, assignment, bundle, or export identity; their high-width lattice/direct-codec work is research-only. Historical FP8_CB_K28..K48 off-law wire ids remain reader-compatible but are excluded from every new menu and assignment. The signed NVFP4_CB_S13..S16 family was DELETED 2026-08-17: it was already research-only here, and Gridbook's native FP4 path is written against the unsigned two-tier product layout (n_sub=2, type_size=4*k+9) with no quality-preserving prefill kernel for n_sub=1, so a signed rung could only ever ride a fallback route. INT4_W4A16 remains a registry-only research format until the approved Gridbook-owned packing/profile/loader/delegation work is implemented and validated. Anything outside the exporter declaration hard-fails rather than silently BF16-coercing a Linear and blowing the allocated byte budget.

format_rules.detail: The generic nvfp4_cb compatibility inventory carries product-VQ NVFP4_CB_K1..K25 (fp4/E2M1 grid, two-tier-v2 serialized body rate 0.40625..3.40625 bpw), product-VQ FP8_CB_K4,K8,...,K48 (fp8/E4M3 grid, 0.5..6.0 index bpw plus the serialized per-output FP32 scale), and the native carriers. AQUA chooses among the formats whose activation contracts the exact target registers; there is no manual NVFP4-versus-FP8 family preference. SM89/RTX40 registers no NVFP4 family and therefore requires FP8, while the maintained SM120/RTX50 surface registers NVFP4 K1..K25 and FP8 but explicitly omits W8A16/source-FP8 compatibility carriers. NVFP4 K26..K32 are unsupported. Historical off-law FP8-CB K28..K48 values remain readable but are not producer formats. Signed S13..S16 remain codec-compatible but are research-only after losing 78.48% (609/776) of matched weight-MSE comparisons, so this production rule excludes them. Plain NVFP4 is W4A4 and FP8_DYNAMIC/FP8-CB are W8A8; comparisons therefore name the full activation/backend contract. FP8_SOURCE, FP8_BLOCK_UE8M0_SOURCE and MXFP4_SOURCE are passthrough-only compatibility carriers and BF16 is unquantized passthrough. The three SOURCE carriers are a FAMILY, not three special cases: each ships the checkpoint's own bytes for the units whose source already IS that format, and allocator_candidates.SOURCE_PASSTHROUGH_CONTRACTS is the one table that says which source kind each requires. That source-kind gate — not this allow-list — is what keeps MXFP4_SOURCE off a bf16 embedding and BF16 off an mxfp4 expert; the entries here only state that the container can carry already-defined source artifacts at all. FP8_BLOCK_UE8M0_SOURCE is the DeepSeek-V3.1/V4 block-FP8 spelling (E4M3 elements, ONE-BYTE UE8M0 block exponents, 8.00049 bpw) and is deliberately distinct from FP8_SOURCE's FP32 weight_scale_inv plane (8.00195 bpw): same element grid, different on-disk contract, different byte count, and FP8_SOURCE's exporter widens its scale plane to FP32, which on a UE8M0 checkpoint would quadruple the scale bytes and emit a tensor the model's own loader does not expect. This allow-list proves only serializer/runtime compatibility; exact target registration plus served KL/PPL and phase-specific performance remain external release gates recorded by the native-parity benchmark protocol.

The nvfp4_cb container's stock compressed-tensors delegation is DENSE-ONLY today: neither export_nvfp4_cb nor the Gridbook runtime carries a stock-CT packed-MoE emission/serving path (35B first-contact, 2026-07-19 — the exporter's stock-NVFP4 global-scale pass is 2-D and Gridbook's MoE method is CB-only). Packed expert stacks use CB rungs (per-expert weighted VQ, served by Gridbook) or the BF16 passthrough until that path is built AND serve-validated. This is a declared capability of the container, not a quality judgement on the formats. MXFP8_UE8M0_G32 joins the list for the SAME structural reason and not as a bpw judgement: its streaming emission is a 2-D dense path (one E4M3 plane plus one float8_e8m0fnu scale plane per Linear) with no packed-expert stacking, so a routed stack has no MXFP8 emission to ship. Its economic exclusion from the routed-expert ladder is a separate and independent fact recorded where the expert cost menu is enumerated (scripts/run_dsv4_mxfp4_cost.sh): at 8.25 bpw it is nearly double the <= 4.25 bpw rungs that menu measures, so it is simply not on it.

MXFP4_SOURCE delegates to the MODEL'S OWN packed-expert loader (DeepseekV4's routed-expert path), which exists only for the routed stack — there is no native packed-MXFP4 load path for a dense attention or shared-expert Linear in this container. On the checkpoints where this matters the source-kind gate already reaches the same verdict (only the routed experts are stored as MXFP4), so this rule is a structural belt on top of a dtype fact, and it fires even on a hypothetical checkpoint that stored a dense Linear in the same packing. It is written as a NAME condition rather than scope=dense deliberately: filter_candidates_for_profile re-checks formats AFTER packed-group aggregation with packed_expert=None, and a scope=dense rule would fire on the aggregated super item (...experts.__packed_serving__...) and strip the format from the very unit it belongs on. The regex still matches that super name, so the deny correctly skips it.

shape_rules.detail: CB rungs pack a 256-weight superblock along the input dim (32 k-bit codewords plus the family-specific serialized scales: production fp4 two-tier v2 is 4k+9 bytes/superblock; fp8 is a 4k-byte index body plus one FP32 scale per output row). The 256-superblock is both the byte-exactness unit and the 8-wide vector-tiling unit; a Linear with in_features % 256 != 0 has no legal CB rung and is masked to another legal candidate. Signed S-rungs stay in this shape contract so legacy/research artifacts remain decodable even though the production format rule excludes them.

Gridbook's fp4-CB N-dimension load gate: the decode/expand kernels and the NVFP4 buffers they write tile the OUTPUT dim in groups of 8 rows, so a Linear with out_features % 8 != 0 has no fp4-CB load path at all. Modelling only the K % 256 superblock rule let the allocator legally assign a rung whose serving lane does not exist (gridbook docs/audits/ultraplan_perf_2026-08-01.md §6, cost-model asymmetry 3); this is the producer-side mirror of that load gate, so the DP can no longer spend budget on an unloadable shape.

Gridbook's fp8-CB N-dimension load gate: the fp8-CB expand/fused prologue writes E4M3 buffers in 16-row output groups (one FP32 weight_scale per output row, packed 16 rows at a time), so a Linear with out_features % 16 != 0 has no fp8-CB load path. The gate is DIFFERENT from the fp4 family's (8) and both are grid facts, not policy — declared per grid from cb_layout's family table so a new rung inherits its family's gate automatically.

serving_lanes.fallback_route: Gridbook fp8_source_w8a16 (added 0.8.5, carried by the pinned 0.8.11): native fp8_source_gemv decode; transient BF16 expansion plus owned grouped BF16 CUTLASS bridge for prefill; stock vLLM routes remain dead on sm121
serving_lanes.detail: SOURCE-PASSTHROUGH lane for the checkpoint's own block-FP8 body: E4M3 elements with ONE-BYTE UE8M0 block exponents at 128x128, copied verbatim. The dedicated Gridbook Fp8SourceW8A16LinearMethod keeps both source planes resident and consumes BF16 activations unchanged; it is not the direct group-32 MXFP8 re-encode lane and does not require GRIDBOOK_MXFP8_DENSE. Numerical pricing is therefore exact zero-cost source passthrough. ROUTE STATUS: BACKED. The evidence is exact Gridbook 0.8.5 commit e992e5980c96333a48149f96392d6cff56ae9e3f and its installed-wheel GB10/sm121 GPU gate (91 passed, 0 skipped), including exact JIT identity/capability and native decode/prefill dispatch. The producer pin advanced to 0.8.11 commit 187c7216b9d4882321c1923de0b4c49dc139743c on 2026-08-21; 0.8.11's packaged contract carries abi_features.source_fp8_block128_w8a16=1 unchanged, so the route stays backed on the attestation, but the GPU gate above has NOT been re-run on 0.8.11. Full-artifact eager/graph generation, native-parity performance and served quality remain independent post-export shipcard gates. Byte contract remains 8.00049 bpw and the wire id remains fp8_e4m3_ue8m0_block128.

route_status_source.detail: Source passthrough still rides a serving route and still needs one attested. Rung-independence does not make it route-free: the W8A16 decode GEMV and the grouped BF16 prefill bridge are distinct routes with distinct predicates.

serving_lanes.fallback_route: vllm Marlin MoE (REQUIRES --moe-backend marlin; the auto default DeepGEMM_MXFP4 asserts on sm121)
serving_lanes.detail: SOURCE-PASSTHROUGH lane for the released checkpoint's own packed routed experts: nibble-packed E2M1 with per-32 E8M0 group scales, copied verbatim, served by the model's native DeepseekV4 routed-expert path rather than by any codebook decoder. Declared as a DISTINCT lane so P5b never files these units under a CB contract they do not have -- a unit here has no CB activation contract at all, which is why the K0.2 attestation scopes itself to CB layers and the artifact declares its source-passthrough units explicitly rather than leaving them looking like a missing attestation. ROUTE STATUS: BACKED, measured on GB10/sm121 2026-08-03 -- native-confirmed via vLLM Marlin MoE. But ONLY off the default: the auto-selected DeepGEMM_MXFP4 backend asserts on the SF transformation, FlashInfer is gated to capability family 100, and the OAI Triton path is hard-excluded on SM12x (0/15 kernels). `--moe-backend marlin` is therefore part of the serving contract, not a tuning hint, and it travels with the artifact in its serving notes. No fused_mid_m block: a passthrough rung has no Gridbook decode prologue to fuse, so an empty backed set is the honest state, not a data gap.

route_status_source.detail: Routed-expert only by this profile's own name rule, and served by the MODEL's packed-expert path behind an operator flag rather than by any codebook decoder. That flag requirement is exactly what route_status='backed_with_serve_flag' plus requires_serve_flags exists to carry in a field a gate can read, instead of the prose below.

serving_lanes.fallback_route: route_unbacked: Gridbook's Mxfp8DenseLinearMethod is OPT-IN behind GRIDBOOK_MXFP8_DENSE=1 and is not default-enabled in the pinned release (verified opt-in at 0.8.5 and again at 0.8.11); with the flag unset a unit declaring this format refuses at load (fail-closed)
serving_lanes.detail: RE-QUANTIZATION lane (not a passthrough): the producer re-encodes any source dtype to E4M3 elements with a float8_e8m0fnu shared exponent per 32 contiguous K, wire id mxfp8_e4m3_e8m0_g32, tensors <unit>.weight + <unit>.weight_scale row-major. ROUTE STATUS: UNBACKED. The consumer-side lane EXISTS and is correctness-audited (gridbook/mxfp8_dense_lane.py, kernel-vs-fp32-oracle over the real DSV4-Flash body shapes on GB10/sm121), but it is opt-in behind GRIDBOOK_MXFP8_DENSE=1 with the NATIVE-PARITY served bench still pending, and Gridbook does not default-enable a lane on correctness evidence alone. This spec's backed set describes what the DEFAULT serve takes, so an operator-flag-gated route is AVAILABLE, NOT BACKED -- the same call nvfp4_cb_quality_path makes about the opt-in fp4 fused mid-M route, and pricing a rung on a lane the default serve never takes is the exact P5b defect this data exists to prevent. NO fused_mid_m KEY, deliberately: a non-CB rung has no CB rung number, so ServingLaneSpec.backed_rungs can never report it backed through that field anyway, and an absent key resolves to the honest 'lane_declares_no_fused_mid_m_lane' source rather than inventing an empty CB ladder. WHEN THIS BECOMES BACKED, key it to the Gridbook version that first RELEASES the lane with the flag defaulted on. Gridbook 0.8.11, the currently pinned release, still keeps this distinct direct-G32 lane opt-in and therefore has no backed entry here; the runtime pin's commit, not a version string alone, binds the consumer code. A pinned version with no entry backs nothing, which is the fail-closed direction. ACTIVATION CONTRACT IS W8A8, not weight-only: the lane quantizes activations dynamically to MXFP8 per 32 reduction-axis elements with the same saturating-ceil rule as the weights (no static global scale, unlike NVFP4). That is why the format's exactness claim on a block-FP8 source is a WEIGHT-PLANE claim (weight_mse == 0.0) and not an output claim, and why cost_entry_is_bit_exact correctly refuses to short-circuit it. Byte contract: 8 + 8/32 = 8.25 bpw exactly, weight plane [N, K] E4M3 plus scale plane [N, K/32] float8_e8m0fnu.

route_status_source.detail: Dense-only emission (a 2-D E4M3 plane plus a scale plane, no packed-expert stacking), and opt-in behind an operator flag in the pinned release.

serving_lanes.detail: The DEFAULT fp4-CB serving contract is NOT W4A4: for all dense M > 8 and all MoE T > 16 the rung expands to BF16 (2 bytes/weight) and feeds an Ampere-schedule grouped GEMM, so the served activation contract is the fp32-emulated group-16 RTN QDQ with a BF16 bridge, and there is no fused mid-M lane at any rung (gridbook ultraplan §2 causes b and c; the true-W4A4 fused kernel stays behind PRISMAQUANT_CB_FUSED_FP4[_MOE] and its six reconsideration gates, so it is deliberately absent from the backed set below). An empty rungs_by_runtime_version means every fp4-CB rung rides the fallback route — which is the honest current state, not a data gap. Gridbook 0.6.0 added a SECOND fp4 fused route that is not the same thing as the one above: a contract-preserving decode-in-prologue mid-M lane (csrc/cb_fused_fp4v2_gemm.cu, dense-only, 9 <= M <= 128, decoded weights bit-identical to cb_expand_v2 at the then-supported 13 K12..K24 rungs so only the FP32 reduction order moves; K1..K11 and K25 require a newer producer-rung-attested Gridbook contract before they are available, while K26..K32 are unsupported). It shipped OPT-IN behind PRISMAQUANT_CB_FP4_FUSED_MIDM=1 pending the served NATIVE-PARITY gate, and with the flag unset the dispatch is byte-for-byte the bridge. It remains opt-in in Gridbook 0.8.11, the version this release pins, with the flag and its gate unchanged (gridbook/fp4v2_fused_midm_lane.py, re-read at 0.8.11). This spec's backed set describes what the DEFAULT contract serves, so it stays EMPTY for every fp4-CB rung: an opt-in route the operator must set an env flag to reach is available, not backed, and pricing a rung on a lane the default serve never takes is the exact P5b defect this data exists to prevent. Revisit only when that lane becomes default. ADDENDUM (Gridbook 0.8.9, 2026-08-18): what an UNSET selector serves on the ROUTED side of this lane changed; the contract did not. PRISMAQUANT_CB_MOE_PERSISTENT_B defaults to auto, so routed CB MoE prefill above the M <= 16 GEMV band takes the contract-preserving persistent-B decode-in-mainloop kernel where its load-time predicate and the extension attest (per-role FP8-CB split books keep the expand+grouped bridge, announced per layer), and PRISMAQUANT_CB_GEMV / PRISMAQUANT_CB_FP8_GEMV_V2 default to auto inside the routed M <= 16 band (v2 only where the compiled occupancy predicate or the exact qualified K28 cell says so). Same activation payload and QDQ as the bridge -- reduction-order-class difference only -- so the sentence above about MoE T > 16 feeding the Ampere-schedule grouped GEMM describes runtimes BEFORE 0.8.9 and the announced fallbacks after it, and this entry's backed set is unchanged: the DENSE fused mid-M lane it prices stays opt-in behind PRISMAQUANT_CB_FP4_FUSED_MIDM. Default-state served evidence: the 0.8.9 default-env KL/PPL leg on the shipped clean 87 GB body vs its gold record, kl_mean +0.17 % / PPL -0.06 % (inside the +/-0.7 % cross-session KL envelope). Gridbook 0.8.10 (tag v0.8.10, exact commit f4b3274722cc0addac60d25c49f9f5306b933937) is 0.8.9 plus a fix for a load regression on split-bank mixed expert stacks (per_expert_format_groups; moe_mixed imported a symbol the tri-state refactor renamed) -- uniform stacks, i.e. every published artifact, were unaffected, and it changes no assignment or default, so the backed set is carried forward UNCHANGED. Gridbook 0.8.11 (tag v0.8.11, exact commit 187c7216b9d4882321c1923de0b4c49dc139743c) is 0.8.10 plus two CUDA-graph capture fixes: gridbook#46 pre-warms the MXFP8 dense lane's swizzled-plane A-side offsets at load so FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture no longer aborts there, and gridbook#47 makes the routed grouped lanes capture-safe -- under capture the fused FP4/FP8 lanes launch the static-capacity tile layout (the PRISMAQUANT_CB_GROUPED_TRIM=0 arm; the trim count is routing-dependent so no captured constant could be right) and the one lane that chunks by host-read per-expert offsets -- the OPT-IN sm12x bridge, PRISMAQUANT_CB_BF16_SM120=1 -- refuses capture naming the flag (the default expand + grouped bridge and the persistent-B lane never host-read and capture as-is). Eager and decode-band (<= 16 tokens) dispatch are byte-identical to 0.8.10; no route, codec, or default changes, so the backed set is carried forward UNCHANGED again. What 0.8.11 changes is WHICH vLLM cudagraph modes can start on a routed CB artifact, not which kernel a regime rides: measured 2026-08-21 on the shipped clean 87 GB body, vLLM's default FULL_AND_PIECEWISE with capture sizes up to 64 starts and serves on 0.8.11 (single-stream decode 20.56-20.64 tok/s, identical to the FULL_DECODE_ONLY [1,2] card command).

route_status_source.detail: fp4-CB rungs land on dense Linears and on routed expert stacks, and Gridbook dispatches the two differently (linear.py vs moe.py), so this lane consults BOTH structural classes of the pinned runtime's eligibility table. It declares the KEY only: the verdict is resolved from the packaged contract by ServingLaneSpec.route_status_for, and per unit at export by cb_route_status_gate. Nothing here may be edited into a verdict -- a hand-typed route status is an assertion, and principle 14 takes assertions about another runtime as refusals. The ROUTE STATUS sentences in this lane's `detail` below are the PROSE this field replaces; they stay as history and explanation, and no gate reads them.

serving_lanes.fallback_route: cb_expand_fp8 -> cutlass_scaled_mm (expand+GEMM, transient E4M3 round trip)
serving_lanes.detail: fp8-CB's fused prologue kernel consumes the SAME per-token dynamic E4M3 QDQ as its non-fused route, so the fused mid-M lane (9 <= M <= 128, measured 1.04x/1.26x/1.45x at M = 32/64/128) is a pure kernel substitution and ships as DEFAULT, but only for the rungs the consumer actually instantiates. The backed set is K in {28,32,36,40,44,48}: k % 4 == 0 is a format-plus-TMA law, because type_size = 4k must be a 16-byte multiple and the fused mainloop's uniform CbSubW = k/4 is wrong for ragged off-law sub-tables. Historical version keys are immutable. Gridbook 0.8.3 added routed per-role LUT support inside the fused mainloop without changing the codec or rung law. Gridbook 0.8.4 explicitly attested abi_features.routed_moe_per_role_codebook_lut=1. The released 0.8.5 rung entry preserves the same codec law and is bound to exact commit e992e5980c96333a48149f96392d6cff56ae9e3f plus the v3 contract. (2026-08-21: the producer pin advanced past 0.8.5 to 0.8.11; that entry stays as written because historical version keys are immutable, and the 0.8.11 key below already carries the identical rung list.) Gridbook 0.8.6 (tag v0.8.6, exact commit dde15e04eb2e3667f78fdacf7b3bc135f0372866) advances the runtime contract to v4 and adds abi_features.dspark_construction_physical_bridge=1 alongside the existing routed_moe_per_role_codebook_lut and source_fp8_block128_w8a16; it integrates DSpark loading and the exact GEMV v2 path. It changes NEITHER the codec NOR the k % 4 == 0 rung law NOR the fused mainloop's CbSubW = k/4, and csrc/cb_fused_gemm.cu is present at that commit, so the backed set is carried forward UNCHANGED rather than widened -- adding the key is what keeps the pin from silently backing nothing, and is not a claim that 0.8.6 serves any rung 0.8.5 did not. Gridbook 0.8.7 (tag v0.8.7, exact commit 98916b0975a174625af5503b04a09d6b270e4419) adds the quantized-embedding serving mechanism and re-audits the vLLM 0.26 dense NVFP4 preflight; its three new routed-MoE kernel lanes are all opt-in and default-off, and gridbook/runtime_contract.py is byte-identical to 0.8.6, so the contract stays v4, the ABI closure is unchanged, and the backed set is again carried forward UNCHANGED rather than widened. Gridbook 0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1, exact commit 227420f9821bab7089632ee914f0ba050f82b817) advances the runtime contract to v12 and the lane table to lane-eligibility v3, and folds in 0.9.0's TP/EP work. Its fused mid-M reader surface is unchanged: gridbook/fp8_fused_lane.py names it (28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48) at that commit -- K28/K32/K36 stay load-compatible optimized paths even though the canonical PRODUCER menu narrowed to K40/K44/K48 in the 0.9.1 ladder retraction, and formats[FP8_CB_K].producer_rungs in the packaged v12 contract says exactly that. Two different sets on the same axis; this key is the reader/dispatch one. So the backed set is carried forward UNCHANGED again rather than widened or narrowed. When the runtime pin advances, ADD its released-version key rather than editing an existing list; an undeclared pinned version backs nothing, fail-closed.

route_status_source.detail: Same key for the fp8-CB family, and the one campaign rule R3 was written for. The shipped DSv4 body's 11 routed FP8-CB layers bind per-role learned codebooks, which Gridbook's persistent-B prefill lane refuses -- a fact no producer-side structure carried, so a user found it at serve time. `role_split` is a per-unit fact that exists only at export, which is why this lane resolves 'unit_dependent' once a table exists and the export gate settles each unit.
